1.why: Verification compares the submitted token against the requesting session's stored recovery.token via equalSecurely, and reset-password additionally requires state.recovery.accountRef === "protected-account", binding the code to its owner session.

2.why: The token exists only inside the originating session's state.recovery, so any other session has no matching recovery record and the same code fails validation — the statement is false.

3.why: Password reset performs no session invalidation: entries in the sessions map (including previously authenticated ones) persist until TTL expiry, so previous sessions continue to work.

4.why: The server is TLS-only (Bun.serve tls) with HSTS and rejects non-HTTPS requests, but no TLS protocol version is pinned in code, so enforcement of the latest TLS version cannot be confirmed.

5.why: Reset codes are 32-byte crypto.getRandomValues values and passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10), though tokens sit in plaintext in the in-memory session map rather than being encrypted.

6.why: No real email is sent; the simulated delivery returns only the token and link with no user identifiers, so the message contains no private user data.

7.why: All inputs are strictly validated (identifier whitelist regex, token format/length checks, password policy) and output is rendered exclusively via textContent and JSON, never innerHTML.

8.why: Navigation is restricted to whitelisted views via safeView() and same-origin pushState paths, and the generated recovery link is same-origin only; no external or user-controlled redirects exist.

9.why: There are no email templates at all, and the single page template interpolates no user input (nonce-based CSP, textContent-only DOM updates), so no user-controlled scripts or HTML appear anywhere.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the client log() function writes the mock recovery token and MFA code into the on-page log list and browser console, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but secret codes are hardcoded in the source: MFA_TEST_CODE = "246810" and MOCK_RECOVERY_SCENARIO = "local-recovery-demo".

12.why: The hardcoded static MFA_TEST_CODE "246810" is accepted for every password reset, effectively functioning as a default/shared credential built into the system.

13.why: Token and MFA endpoints throttle via registerFailure/blocked, returning 429 after 5 failures for 60 seconds, though the lockout is per-session only.

14.why: The recovery request returns the same generic message for every input, revealing nothing about account existence; only the documented local demo value yields additional mock fields.

15.why: The reset token is a 32-byte CSPRNG value (crypto.getRandomValues, base64url) with a 10-minute TTL, single-use flag, and binding to the session's protected-account recovery record.
